lines: I still <pulse>remember</pulse> you trying to take my {stolen_stack}.
That {stolen_item} from the {stolen_container}, I have not forgotten.
You put your hands on village stores once. I am <pulse>watching</pulse> them now.
Trust is counted in small things. Last time, it was counted in {stolen_stack}.
I remember the {stolen_container}, the missing {stolen_item}, and your face beside both.
If you came to make right with the {stolen_item}, start by keeping your hands visible.
The {stolen_stack} was not yours, and pretending otherwise will not help you here.
I keep my things closer now. You can guess why.
A stolen {stolen_item} leaves more behind than an empty space.
Speak if you need to, but understand why I am still <shake>careful</shake>.
I moved the valuable supplies after what happened.
The empty place in that container was easy to notice.
I check the latch twice whenever you are nearby.
Returning what you took would be a useful start.
I know exactly how many {stolen_item} belonged there.
People worked for those supplies before you reached for them.
The theft made ordinary conversation harder than it should be.
I have not decided whether you regret taking it.
Keep away from the {stolen_container} while we talk.
An apology will need honest actions behind it.
<aqua>{theft_witness}</aqua> told me about you stealing {stolen_stack}. Not wise.
Word travels faster than full pockets. <aqua>{theft_witness}</aqua> <pulse>saw</pulse> the {stolen_item}.
Around here, a missing {stolen_item} becomes everybody's story.
<aqua>{theft_witness_possessive}</aqua> <shake>warning</shake> reached more doors than you opened.
People here share bread, tools, and warnings. After that {stolen_stack}, you became the warning.
I was not there, but <aqua>{theft_witness}</aqua> was. That is enough for me to watch the {stolen_container}.
A theft from one villager has a way of reaching every counter in the village.
You may think {stolen_stack} was a small thing. Villages do not measure trust that way.
The story of that {stolen_item} arrived before you did.
I will speak with you, but I will also keep one eye on my <pulse>stores</pulse>.
The whole market heard about the missing {stolen_item}.
I know which container was opened and who was seen beside it.
Nobody needed to embellish the story for it to sound bad.
The traders started counting their stock after the warning spread.
You made several villagers nervous about leaving supplies unattended.
I trust <aqua>{theft_witness}</aqua> to know what they saw.
The missing item became village business when you refused to return it.
Do not expect the other shopkeepers to ignore that warning.
People have started closing their shutters when you approach.
If the story is wrong, your conduct from here must prove it.
